questions.q_en: Name a common electrolyte disorder that occurs when the amount of sodium in your blood becomes abnormally low.
questions.solution_en: Hyponatremia is a condition where the sodium levels in the blood drop below normal (less than 135 mEq/L), leading to symptoms like nausea, headaches, confusion, and seizures.

questions.q_en: Which amino acid is a precursor to serotonin, a neurotransmitter that regulates your appetite, sleep and mood?
questions.solution_en:
• The amino acid tryptophan is the precursor to serotonin, a neurotransmitter that plays a crucial role in regulating mood, appetite, and sleep.

• Serotonin's influence extends beyond the central nervous system; it is also synthesized in the intestines, where it regulates gut motility and secretory activity

questions.q_en: Select the INCORRECT statement with regards to vitamins.
options_en: Plants can synthesise almost all vitamins.
Most of the vitamins cannot get synthesised in sufficient amount in our body.
Some bacteria in the gut do not produce vitamins.
questions.solution_en:
• Statement D is incorrect as gut bacteria, like those producing vitamin K and some B vitamins, do synthesize vitamins.

• Statements A, B, and C are correct: plants synthesize most vitamins, humans cannot produce sufficient amounts of most vitamins, and vitamins are organic compounds.

Further Insight:

• Vitamins are essential micronutrients required in small amounts for metabolic processes. Deficiencies can cause diseases like scurvy (vitamin C) or beriberi (vitamin B1).

• Gut bacteria contribute significantly to vitamin K and B vitamin production, reducing dependency on dietary sources.
questions.solution_hi:
• कथन D गलत है क्योंकि आंत के बैक्टीरिया, जैसे विटामिन K व कुछ B विटामिन उत्पन्न करने वाले, विटामिन संश्लेषित करते हैं।

• कथन A, B व C सही हैं: पौधे अधिकांश विटामिन संश्लेषित करते हैं, मनुष्य अधिकांश विटामिनों की पर्याप्त मात्रा उत्पन्न नहीं कर सकते, व विटामिन कार्बनिक यौगिक हैं।

questions.q_en: ______ is the tube that carries urine from the kidney to the urinary bladder.
questions.solution_en:
The major organs of the urinary system are:

Kidneys - filter the blood, keep the right balance of water in body tissues, and change liquid wasteproducts into urine.

Ureters - long narrow tubes that carry urine from the kidneys to the urinary bladder.

Urinary bladder - a muscular pouch where urine collects and is stored until it is passed out of the body.

Urethra - short, narrow tube that carries urine from the bladder to the outside.

questions.q_en: Swollen bluish veins resulting from the valves that do not close properly are called _____.
questions.solution_en: Varicose veins are twisted, swollen veins near the surface of the skin and occur when weak or defective valves allow blood to flow backward or stagnate within the vein.

Column-A (Food component)Column-B (Enzyme involved in digestion)

questions.q_en:
Which of the following are the functions of blood in the human body?

1) Oxygen transport

2) Carbon dioxide transport

3) Nutrient transport

4) Waste disposal

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.solution_en:
Waste disposal is not a function of blood. Blood plays several important roles in the body, including:

• Oxygen transport: Blood carries oxygen from the lungs to the cells in the body and also carries carbon dioxide from the cells to the lungs for removal.

• Carbon dioxide transport: Blood carries carbon dioxide away from the cells and to the lungs, where it is exhaled.

• Nutrient transport: Blood carries nutrients such as glucose, amino acids, and minerals from the digestive system to the cells of the body.

questions.q_en: What do you mean by semiconservative DNA replication?
options_en: After the completion of replication, each DNA molecule would have two parental and two newly synthesised strands.
RNA is dependent on DNA for the synthesis of proteins.
DNA is dependent on RNA for the synthesis of proteins.
After the completion of replication, each DNA molecule would have one parental and one newly synthesised strand.
questions.solution_en:
Semiconservative DNA replication is a process discovered by Meselson and Stahl in 1958, where each new DNA molecule formed during replication consists of one parental (original) strand and one newly synthesized strand. During replication, the double-stranded DNA unwinds, and each strand serves as a template for the synthesis of a complementary strand. This ensures that the genetic information is preserved, with each daughter molecule being half "old" (parental) and half "new."

· Option 1 is incorrect because it suggests four strands per molecule, which contradicts the structure of DNA (only two strands per molecule).

· Options 2 and 3 describe transcription and reverse transcription, respectively, not replication.

· Option 4 correctly defines semiconservative replication.

Thus, the correct answer is option 4.

questions.q_en: Which of the following glands is present between the lungs?
questions.solution_en:
The thymus gland, located behind your sternum and between your lungs, is only active until puberty.

After puberty, the thymus starts to slowly shrink and become replaced by fat.

Thymosin is the hormone of the thymus, and it stimulates the development of disease-fighting T cells.

The thymus gland will not function throughout a full lifetime, but it has a big responsibility when it's active - helping the body protect itself against autoimmunity, which occurs when the immune system turns against itself. Therefore, the thymus plays a vital role in the lymphatic system (your body's defense network) and endocrine system.

questions.q_en:
Which of the following statements about enzymes in the human body is/are correct?

Statement A: Maltase is present in the saliva and breaks the sugar maltose into glucose.

Statement B: Amylase is present in the saliva and helps change starches into sugars.
questions.solution_en:
Statement A: Maltase is present in the saliva and breaks the sugar maltose into glucose.

· This is incorrect. Maltase is an enzyme that breaks down maltose into glucose, but it is primarily found in the small intestine, not in saliva. Saliva contains enzymes like amylase (also called ptyalin), but not maltase.

Statement B: Amylase is present in the saliva and helps change starches into sugars.

· This is correct. Salivary amylase, also known as ptyalin, is present in saliva and begins the digestion of starches by breaking them down into simpler sugars like maltose.

Further insight:

Digestive Enzymes in the Human Body

1) Mouth:

o Enzymes: Salivary amylase (ptyalin) and lingual lipase.

o Function: Salivary amylase breaks down starches into simpler sugars like maltose. For example, when you chew bread, it starts tasting sweeter as starches are converted into sugars. Lingual lipase begins fat digestion but is more active in the stomach.

o Conditions: Saliva has a near-neutral pH (around 6.2 - 7.6), which is optimal for amylase activity.

2) Stomach:

o Enzymes: Pepsin (for proteins) and gastric lipase (for fats). Salivary amylase is deactivated here due to the low pH (1.5 - 3.5).

o Function: The stomach primarily digests proteins using pepsin, and no significant carbohydrate digestion occurs here. Maltase is not present in the stomach either.

3) Small Intestine:

o Enzymes: Pancreatic amylase, brush border enzymes (maltase, sucrase, lactase, etc.), and others like trypsin and lipase.

o Function:

§ Pancreatic amylase continues starch digestion, breaking starches into maltose.

§ Brush border enzymes like maltase, sucrase (breaks sucrose into glucose and fructose), and lactase (breaks lactose into glucose and galactose) complete carbohydrate digestion.

§ The resulting monosaccharides (glucose, fructose, galactose) are absorbed into the bloodstream through the intestinal lining.

o Conditions: The small intestine has a slightly alkaline pH (around 7 - 8), ideal for these enzymes.

4) Large Intestine:

o No significant enzymatic digestion occurs here, but gut bacteria ferment undigested carbohydrates, producing gases and short-chain fatty acids.

questions.q_en: Which of the following organ secretes hydrochloric acid that helps our body in killing pathogenic bacteria?
questions.solution_en: Stomach secretes hydrochloric acid that helps our body in killing pathogenic bacteria. It is secreted by parietal cells in the stomach.Excessive secretion of stomach acid can lead to the formation of peptic ulcers.

questions.q_en: From which of the following sources does the brain get energy?
questions.solution_en: Brain get energy from glucose. Glucose, a form of sugar, is the primary source of energy for every cell in the body. Because the brain is so rich in nerve cells, or neurons, it is the most energy-demanding organ, using one-half of all the sugar energy in the body.

questions.q_en: Which part of the body is responsible for the manufacture of red blood cells?
questions.solution_en: Bone marrow produces red blood cells that carry oxygen, white blood cells that prevent infection and platelets that control bleeding. The absence of bone marrow can be fatal since it's an essential part of your body. Bone marrow is spongy tissue in the middle of certain bones. Most blood cells are made in your bone marrow. This process is called haemopoiesis.

questions.solution_en: Iron is a mineral found in every cell of the body. Iron is considered an essential mineral because it is needed to make hemoglobin, a part of blood cells.

questions.q_en: Which of the following chemicals is responsible for the yellow in urine?
questions.solution_en: The most common color of urine is yellow, which is caused by the presence of urobilin , a biochemical waste product generated from the breakdown of old red blood cells. (Your body makes about 2 million new red blood cells every day, and recycles an equal number of old ones.)
